avatar-has-kind.summary: An avatar for a kind nothing declares. Not a defect — the vocabulary is open and a folio may declare it — but it is how a registry drifts away from the instances that use it, so it is reported rather than pruned.

kind-has-avatar.summary: Every declared kind has an avatar of its own. A kind with none renders as the generic question mark — deliberately a gap rather than a neutral mark, because a reader must be able to tell "no art yet" from "this is what it looks like".

trash-state-derived.summary: The trash state is composed from the base glyph rather than drawn per kind, so its coverage cannot lag. Asserted ONCE: a per-kind criterion here could never fail, which would read as coverage while measuring nothing.
